A 38-year-old woman seeks medical attention for a one-month duration of dull right knee pain without
any history of trauma or changes in activity level. During examination, she shows mild discomfort while
mounting the examination table. Physical examination reveals right-sided superior ASIS, right-sided
inferior PSIS, and left-sided superior ischial tuberosity. A positive standing flexion test is noted on the
right side. Bilateral radiographic imaging of the knee, hip, and pelvis shows no pathological findings.
Which muscle is most likely responsible for this somatic dysfunction pattern? Answer Choices: (A)
Tensor fasciae latae (B) Piriformis (C) Adductor magnus (D) Rectus femoris (E) Sartorius (F) Biceps
femoris (G) Gluteus maximus (H) Iliacus (I) Vastus medialis (J) Semitendinosus
 A. Sartorius
B. Piriformis
C. Semitendinosus
D. Vastus medialis
E. Rectus femoris
F. Tensor fasciae latae
G. Iliacus
H. Gluteus maximus
I. Adductor magnus
J. Biceps femoris
